seo.title: Affiliated Organizations · Ontario Rare Action Group
seo.description: Many rare disease organizations across Ontario partner with us on advocacy, research and patient support and we are adding new partners all the time. Together, we are stronger.

header.title: We do this work together.
header.lede: Many rare disease organizations across Ontario partner with us on advocacy, research and patient support. Each one brings deep expertise in their condition area — together, we represent more than a million Ontarians.

partners.name: Canadian Organization for Rare Disorders
partners.focus: National advocacy network and umbrella body for Canada's rare-disease patient groups.

partners.name: National Organization for Rare Disorders (US)
partners.focus: Cross-border partner for research, registries and policy benchmarking.

partners.name: Rare Disease Foundation of Ontario
partners.focus: Microgrant research funding for under-studied conditions affecting Ontario families.
The Canadian Addison Society provides advocacy, education, and support for Canadians with Adrenal Disorders

partners.name: ALS Society of Canada
partners.focus: The ALS Society of Canada is working to change what it means to live with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), an unrelenting and currently terminal disease.

partners.name: Canadian Arthritis Patient Alliance
partners.focus: CAPA uses the power of information, research, and communication to help people living with arthritis find their voice and support others.

partners.name: Canadian XLH Network
partners.focus: A Canadian patient support organization for people living and dealing with X-Linked Hypophosphatemia (XLH)

partners.name: Canadian Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation
partners.focus: The Canadian Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation is committed to accelerating research, empowering our community, and transforming care so that everyone with pulmonary fibrosis can live a better life.

partners.name: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Society of Canada
partners.focus: CML Society of Canada is dedicated to supporting and advocating for patients with chronic myeloid leukemia.

partners.name: Cystic Fibrosis Canada
partners.focus: Cystic Fibrosis Canada is a national charitable organization founded in 1960 that funds research, supports the CF community, and advocates for improved access to treatments across Canada.
Defeat Duchenne Canada is dedicated to ending Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

partners.name: Histiocytosis Association of Canada
partners.focus: The Histiocytosis Association of Canada is dedicated to improving the lives of Canadians affected by histiocytosis
Our mission is to be a patient-centric organization focused on finding a cure for IgA Nephropathy.

partners.name: Mito Canada
partners.focus: We support Canadians living with or at risk of mitochondrial disease, along with their families, caregivers, healthcare providers, and researchers.

partners.name: Muscular Dystrophy Canada
partners.focus: Muscular Dystrophy Canada works with individuals and families affected by neuromuscular disorders to eliminate the obstacles that can limit access, opportunity, and independence.

partners.name: Canadian Transverse Myelitis Association
partners.focus: The CTMA was created to support and create a networking infrastructure for patients and their families; to provide relevant information about the latest findings in research and treatments; and promote public awareness of the rare neuroimmunologic disorders of the central nervous system

partners.name: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (aHUS) Canada
partners.focus: aHUS Canada is a not-for-profit organization. Formed in November 2012, the mission of the organization is to support patients and families living with atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome.

partners.name: ALD Hope
partners.focus: ALD Hope is dedicated to raising awareness of X-linked Adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) and Addison's disease (Adrenal insufficiency), and advocating for ALD newborn screening.

partners.name: ALS Action Canada
partners.focus: ALS Action Canada, Canada’s only national, patient-driven organization, connects and raises the voices of those most impacted by ALS to increase affordable patient care, and advance trials, treatments and research toward a cure.

partners.name: Angelman Syndrome Foundation Canada
partners.focus: ASF Canada provides essential access to resources, connection for emotional and physical wellbeing, fuel for innovation, research and world class clinical care while advocating for all---resulting in full and meaningful lives for everyone touched by AS.

partners.name: Canadian FOP Network
partners.focus: The Canadian FOP Network (CFOPN) is non-profit volunteer organization made up of parents of children with Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP), youth and adults with FOP, caregivers, family members and friends.

SPG50 is a Ultra-Rare Neurodegenerative disease that slowly takes away children with the diseases ability to use their legs, hands and mental capacity. CureSPG50 is working with the world top scientists, labs and hospitals to make a Gene Therapy for SPG50.
The PKD Foundation of Canada is dedicated to fighting polycystic kidney disease through research, education, advocacy, support, and awareness.

partners.name: Genetic Aortic Disorders Association Canada
partners.focus: GADA is dedicated to saving lives and enabling a promising future for individuals living with Marfan syndrome and other genetic aortic disorders through education, awareness, support and research.

partners.name: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome Association of Canada
partners.focus: The Li-Fraumeni Syndrome Association of Canada (LFSA-Canada) supports families affected by LFS, promotes awareness, and collaborates with researchers and medical professionals to improve screening and care.

partners.name: Canadian MPS Society
partners.focus: Mucopolysaccharidoses (MPSs) are rare genetic disorders in children and adults. The Canadian MPS Society supports families, raises awareness, and funds research to improve lives affected by MPS, offering advocacy, resources, and hope.

partners.name: Pulmonary Hypertension Association of Canada
partners.focus: PHA Canada is a federally registered charity established in 2008 by patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals to work together to better the lives of Canadians affected by pulmonary hypertension and represent a united national PH community.

The Canadian Association for Porphyria (CAP) is dedicated to providing support, information, and advocacy for individuals affected by porphyria across Canada.

partners.name: Sickle Cell Society of Canada
partners.focus: Patient support, education and equity advocacy for the sickle-cell community.

partners.name: Muscular Dystrophy Canada
partners.focus: Service, research and advocacy for over 160 neuromuscular conditions.

partners.name: Cystic Fibrosis Canada
partners.focus: Funding research and advocating for affordable access to CF therapies.

partners.name: Huntington Society of Canada
partners.focus: Resources, research and advocacy for Huntington's disease families.

partners.name: Pulmonary Hypertension Association Canada
partners.focus: Patient support and treatment-access advocacy for the PH community.

partners.name: Cure SMA Canada
partners.focus: Family support and access advocacy for spinal muscular atrophy.

partners.name: Wilson Disease Association, Canada Chapter
partners.focus: Advocacy for Wilson disease.

becomePartner.title: Run a rare-disease organization in Ontario? Let's talk.
becomePartner.body: We host a quarterly leaders' roundtable, share advocacy updates, and amplify member campaigns. Affiliation is free.
